title: Normalized comparison of the two ordinary finite coefficient pullbacks
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell and a morphism g:X→Y of schemes on which ell is invertible. Use finiteIntegral_n, finiteCompleted_n and FiniteNormalization of [def-pod-integral-completed-comparison-data]. For every n≥0, there is a natural module isomorphism e_n:finiteIntegral_n≅finiteCompleted_n preserving the specified pulled quotient-unit generators. This is an underived assertion about modules; it has no chosen strict derived tower, derived inverse limit or completeness hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 03EK/03EL, sheafified tensor and pullback tensor association; finite-generator portion of proetale.tex Tag 099N(5) and of lem-a1-completed-integral-finite-tower-transport, proof steps 1-2.

proof.text: Use the unique coefficient isomorphisms preserving integral constants to identify the positive quotient rings and their completed projections. The projection squares are commutative by their sectionwise coefficient formulas.

Inverse image preserves these isomorphisms. Associate scalar extension with inverse image: both functors become the sheafification of the balanced inverse-image tensor over the same quotient. The map is the same pure tensor under the coefficient identifications, and its inverse uses the inverse coefficient identifications. The projection squares imply balancing; the formulas commute with restrictions and module arrows. Sheafification gives natural inverse isomorphisms at every level.

Both tensor maps preserve 1, so their value on the generator integralOperationsPullbackGenerator(1 tensor x) is completedReductionFiniteGenerator(1,1,x). This is exactly FiniteNormalization. The zero module and empty site satisfy the same formulas; the exponent is always n+1, so n=0 uses the first positive quotient.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteIntegral_coefficientComparison
    (hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (l : Y.presheaf.stalk y)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ n : ℕ, finiteIntegral l E g n ≅ finiteCompleted l E g n,
      ∀ n : ℕ, FiniteNormalization l E g n (e n)
